previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with fever and hypotension during dialysis, found to have MSSA bacteremia likely from his right femoral dialysis catheter. He was treated with vancomycin initially, then transitioned to cefazolin after sensitivities confirmed susceptibility. The infected catheter was removed, and after a 5-day line holiday, a new tunneled left femoral dialysis catheter was placed. Blood cultures cleared, and he completed dialysis without complications. His heart function remained stable, and no endocarditis was detected. New medications were started, including lisinopril for heart failure, atorvastatin, and adjusted phosphate binders. He was discharged to an extended care facility on outpatient antibiotics with plans for ongoing dialysis and follow-up.

INDICATION:  ___ male with end-stage renal disease and tunneled left
femoral dialysis line presenting with Staph bacteremia.  Request for catheter
removal with culture of the line tip.

OPERATORS:  The procedure was performed by Dr. ___ (fellow).  Dr.
___ attending radiologist, reviewed the study.  

PROCEDURE AND FINDINGS:  A timeout was performed with two patient identifiers.
The patient's indwelling dialysis catheter and left groin were prepped and
draped in usual sterile fashion.  Approximately 10 cc of lidocaine was
administered to the tunneled site.  Blunt dissection was performed around the
catheter cuff.  Gentle pressure was used to remove the catheter and pressure
was placed at the left common femoral venous entry site for approximately ten
minutes.  A sterile dressing was applied over the puncture site.  The tip of
the catheter was sent for culture.  There were no post-procedural
complications.

IMPRESSION:  Successful removal of a tunneled left common femoral hemodialysis
catheter.  The tip was sent for culture.

CLINICAL HISTORY:  ___ male with end-stage renal disease on
hemodialysis, presenting with sepsis.  Request for placement of a temporary
femoral HD line with VIP port.

OPERATORS:  The procedure was performed by Dr. ___ (fellow).  Dr.
___, the attending radiologist, supervised and reviewed the
study.

ANESTHESIA:  1% local lidocaine.  The patient's hemodynamic parameters were
continuously monitored throughout the course of the procedure.

PROCEDURE:  After the risks, benefits and alternatives of the procedure were
explained to the patient, informed consent was obtained.  The patient was
brought to the angiographic suite and his right groin was prepped and draped
in the usual sterile fashion.  A preprocedure timeout and huddle were
performed as per ___ protocol.

Under ultrasound guidance with hard copy images on file, the right common
femoral vein was accessed with a 19-gauge needle over the femoral head.  A
___ wire was advanced into the IVC and serial dilatations were performed
over the wire.  A 12 ___ peel-away sheath was then placed over the wire and
the guidewire and inner dilator were removed.  A new 12 ___ dual-lumen
hemodialysis catheter with VIP port measuring 20 cm in length was advanced
over the wire and the wire was removed.  All three ports were aspirated and
flushed easily.  The catheter was secured to the skin with 0 silk suture and a
sterile dressing was applied.  A final fluoroscopic image was saved digitally
and confirmed satisfactory position of the catheter with the tip terminating
in the proximal right common iliac vein.

The patient tolerated the procedure well and there were no immediate
complications.

IMPRESSION:  Successful placement of a 12 ___ dual-lumen temporary dialysis
catheter with VIP port measuring 20 cm in length via right common femoral
venous access. The line is ready for use.

INDICATION:  New oxygen requirement.  Questionable volume overload.

COMPARISON:  ___.

FINDINGS:  As compared to the previous examination, the technical quality is

MEDICAL HISTORY:  ___ man with end-stage renal disease and MRSA
bacteremia.  A left tunneled femoral dialysis catheter was removed about a
week ago and a temporary right femoral HD catheter was removed two days ago. 
Patient has a history of central occlusion of the veins in the neck and upper
chest.  A femoral tunneled hemodialysis catheter placement was requested.

COMPARISON:  Multiple similar procedures in the past.

CLINICIANS:  Dr. ___, Dr. ___, and Dr. ___.  Dr.
___ is the attending radiologist who was present and supervising
throughout.

ANESTHESIA:  Moderate sedation was provided by administering divided doses of
200 mcg of fentanyl and 2.5 mg of Versed throughout the total intra-service
time of 1 hour 30 minutes, during which the patient's hemodynamic parameters
were continuously monitored.  Local anesthesia with 1% lidocaine and lidocaine
with epinephrine.

PROCEDURE AND FINDINGS:  An informed written consent was obtained after
explaining the procedure, benefits, alternatives and risks involved.  Patient
was brought to angiography suite and placed supine on the imaging table.  The
left groin was prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.  A
preprocedure huddle and timeout were performed as per ___ protocol.

Under ultrasound and fluoroscopic guidance with hard copy images of ultrasound
on file, the left common femoral vein was accessed with a micropuncture set. 
Through the micropuncture sheath, a 0.035 ___ wire was placed and advanced
into right atrium.  Appropriate measurements were then obtained for the
catheter length.  Then after instilling 1% lidocaine with epinephrine, a small
incision was made over the anterolateral upper thigh.  From this incision, a
50-cm tip-to-cuff tunneled hemodialysis catheter was placed and brought out at
the venotomy site using the tunneling device.  Then after removing the
micropuncture sheath, the soft tissue tract was dilated with serial dilators
over the guidewire.  A peel-away sheath was placed over the guidewire.  The
inner dilator and guidewire were removed and the catheter was placed through
the peel-away sheath and advanced into right atrium.  The peel-away sheath was
then removed.  Catheter secured to skin with 0 silk sutures and venotomy site
closed with ___ Vicryl suture.  Both ports of the catheter were easily
aspirated and flushed.  A fluoroscopic spot chest film was obtained
demonstrating satisfactory position and placement of the catheter with the tip
terminating in the right atrium.  Sterile dressings were applied.  Patient
tolerated the procedure well and there were no immediate complications.

IMPRESSION:  Successful placement of a tunneled hemodialysis catheter
measuring 50 cm tip-to-cuff via left common femoral venous access with the tip
of the catheter terminating in the right atrium.  The line is ready for use.
